_comment: 📇️ Test-only oracle registry. An oracle is a third-party reference implementation used ONLY by the test/oracle host to produce the reference projection a repository implementation is compared against. Nothing here may appear in a production manifest or be reachable from a production target — `bun ./📜️script.ts dependency check` enforces that. Exact resolved versions and checksums live in the ecosystem lockfile, not here.

oracles.rationale: Typed, step-by-step PDF writer with explicit control over catalog, page tree, media boxes and content streams — the creation reference. Deterministic given the same call sequence, no network, no system dependencies, runs on Windows/macOS/Linux.

PDF document-manipulation library exposing object-level editing, page insert/delete, content-stream rewriting and an independent parser — serves both as the editing oracle and as the independent reader that proves a subject's output is parseable.

The de-facto specification of recursive class-name flattening: nested arrays, truthy object keys, falsey suppression and numeric coercion. Deterministic, dependency-free, no network, no system dependencies, runs on every platform. Deliberately scoped to the FLATTENING half of the repository's cn() — clsx knows nothing about conflicting utility families, so it is not, and must not be used as, an oracle for conflict resolution.

The published contract that this repository's styleVariants() re-implements: base class, finite variant schema, defaultVariants, boolean choices, compoundVariants with array conditions, and caller class/className overrides. Deterministic, dependency-light, no network. Valid only over UNCLASSIFIED class tokens: styleVariants() finishes through cn(), which additionally resolves repository-owned utility conflicts that cva knows nothing about — the vectors are scoped accordingly.

The reference PNG encoder/decoder of the Rust ecosystem, and an INDEPENDENT reader for this repository's own encoder. Deterministic for a fixed colour type, bit depth and filter setting, no network, no system dependencies, cross-platform. Scoped to the normative surface: dimensions, colour model, bit depth and decoded samples — filter selection, interlacing and ancillary chunks are encoder freedom and are canonicalized away by semantic-raster-v1.

productionDebt.plan: The OS host rasterizes SVG to PNG through this crate, so it is production-reachable TODAY. Discovered by the oracle-purity gate when png was registered — the gate did its job. Phase 7 target: the rasterizer's PNG writing belongs behind ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio's own encode_png, at which point this entry loses its productionDebt and testOnly becomes a fact.

oracles.rationale: The reference GIF encoder/decoder of the Rust ecosystem. GIF is palette-based, so exact RGBA is a quantizer choice; the oracle is used only for frame geometry, frame count and opaque-sample structure, which the format does fix.

The reference ZIP reader/writer of the Rust ecosystem, and an independent reader for this repository's own writer. Entry order, compression method and level, timestamps and external attributes are writer freedom; member names, uncompressed sizes and content digests are normative and are what semantic-archive-v1 compares.

productionDebt.plan: The OS host declares an optional `zip` dependency for container handling, so it is production-reachable TODAY. Phase 7 target: route that through ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio's own encode_zip/decode_zip.

oracles.rationale: The reference zlib/deflate implementation of the Rust ecosystem. RFC 1951 does not fix WHICH encoding a compressor chooses, so this oracle is deliberately used for the ROUND TRIP — an independent inflater must recover exactly what this repository deflated — never for byte equality.

The reference RIFF/PCM WAVE reader/writer of the Rust ecosystem, and an independent reader for this repository's own writer. Chunk padding, LIST/INFO metadata and chunk order are writer freedom; the format block and the decoded samples are normative.
The reference RFC 4180 CSV reader/writer of the Rust ecosystem. Line terminator, quote style and trailing newline are writer freedom; the header and the cell grid are normative.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: The repository test platform is the thing under test; no third-party library implements this repository's taxonomy, feature profile or cache contract, so an external reference would be meaningless. Confidence comes from specification vectors (the frozen contract), metamorphic laws (discovery is idempotent, clean is a no-op on a clean tree) and independently written assertions per behaviour.

cn() resolves conflicts over a finite table of REPOSITORY-OWNED utility families (ui-surface/ui-glass/ui-veil fills, px-single/px-tiny spacing, text-element sizing, border-accent colours). tailwind-merge and every other third-party merger resolve against Tailwind's default scale and know none of these families, so agreeing with one would prove nothing and disagreeing with it would prove nothing either. Choosing such a library purely to satisfy the workflow would be selecting a weak oracle mechanically. The group table in 🟦️component.ts is the specification, and the vectors in the feature carry it.
